source_text: Iam ergo ea quae contexuit lacerator naturalium, ponderemus; sed ut rerum, quae mutua sunt responsione perplexae, lectori nostro tam intellegentia quam discretio suggeratur, quo genere obluctetur, admoneo. Profitetur scriptis obviare nostris, quae ad se ait in brevi chartula destinata, et ponit aliquas sententiarum mearum particulas atque suggillat, quae in meo opere non tenentur.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore let us weigh those things which the tearer of natural things has woven together; but so that both understanding and discernment of matters which are entangled by mutual reply may be supplied to our reader, I advise by what kind of fighting he struggles. He professes to meet our writings, which he says were sent to him on a short sheet, and he sets down some little pieces of my sentences and brands them, which are not held in my work.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: Let us now weigh the things this slanderer of nature has put together. But to help our reader both understand and distinguish matters entangled in our replies to one another, I will explain the way he fights. He professes to answer writings of mine that he says were sent to him on a short sheet, and he quotes and attacks little pieces of statements attributed to me that are not found in my work.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
